extraction.name: MathVista
extraction.description: A benchmark dataset for evaluating mathematical reasoning of foundation models in visual contexts, consisting of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA).
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data collected from 28 existing multimodal datasets (9 MathQA datasets and 19 VQA datasets) and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA). Existing datasets were limited to 400 examples each to ensure balanced representation. VQA datasets underwent automatic filtration followed by manual labeling by expert annotators to identify mathematical reasoning examples.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: A preliminary study of 200 examples shows that GPT-4 can extract the answer text with more than 99.5% accuracy. Annotations were sourced from original data providers, resulting in only 85.6% of examples (Table 1) having annotations. Due to the heterogeneity of these sources, annotations lack a unified format and structure.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 28 existing multimodal datasets including MathQA datasets (Geometry3K, GeoQA+, GEOS, UniGeo, CLEVR-Math, IconQA, TabMWP, SciBench, TheoremQA) and VQA datasets (ChartQA, FigureQA, DVQA, MapQA, PlotQA, DocVQA, AI2D, ScienceQA, TQA, A-OKVQA, KVQA, ParsVQA-Caps, TextVQA, VizWiz, VQA2.0, PMC-VQA, VQA-RAD, Super-CLEVR, VQA-AS). Three newly created datasets: IQTest (228 examples from puzzle test figures on online learning platforms), FunctionQA (400 examples on functional plots), PaperQA (107 examples from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Papers released in August 2023 for PaperQA subset
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: We adopted this sampling strategy: (1) first, randomly sample questions with a threshold number of 4 for each source dataset; (2) then, randomly sample the remaining questions for each source dataset on its proportion in the entire set. Each source dataset is limited to up to 400 examples to ensure a balanced representation of each source in our final compiled benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Automatic selection using heuristic rules to filter examples with numeric answers or quantity words, followed by manual labeling by three expert annotators using majority voting. Each source dataset limited to 400 examples maximum. Quality checks conducted to address unidentified errors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: All questions for the three new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA) were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields. A two-step annotation process was employed: initial independent annotation by three reviewers, followed by discussion among the entire review team to resolve discrepancies. Metadata annotations (question type, answer type, task, grade level, visual context, mathematical reasoning) were obtained from source dataset details and verified through manual labeling of 1,000 examples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom GUI annotation tool, Amazon Mechanical Turk for human performance evaluation and Multimodal Bard assessment
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-annotation consistency rate of 99.2% achieved among three reviewers for the newly collected 736 questions, with only 6 disagreements. Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775 for mathematical reasoning labeling indicates substantial consistency. Discrepancies resolved through team discussion to reach consensus.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 annotators for new datasets, 5 annotators for human performance evaluation
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Graduate students in STEM fields for new dataset annotation. For human performance evaluation: annotators with satisfactory annotating history (>5,000 HIT tasks completed, acceptance score >0.99), high school diploma or higher education level.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: EasyOCR for OCR text detection, Multimodal Bard for image caption generation
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Dataset divided into testmini (1,000 examples for model development) and test (5,141 examples for standard evaluation). Answer labels for test set will not be publicly released to prevent data contamination. Online evaluation platform will be maintained. Commitment to evolving the leaderboard and maintaining datasets in response to community feedback.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Grade level information (elementary school, high school, college) is collected as metadata for questions.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark aims to facilitate development of general-purpose AI agents capable of tackling mathematically intensive and visually rich real-world tasks, with applications in educational disciplines, data analysis, and scientific discovery.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset's focus on mathematical reasoning within visual contexts, spanning specific domains like science and college-level math, necessitates a more labor-intensive process for collecting high-quality data compared to textual-only or general-purpose datasets. While MathVista encompasses a broad spectrum of tasks and visual contexts, there may be gaps in the representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. The scalability and generalizability of our benchmark to other domains remain a concern.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Dataset coverage gaps exist in representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. Focus on specific domains (science, college-level math) requires labor-intensive data collection. Only 85.6% of examples have annotations due to heterogeneous sources. Annotations lack unified format and structure across sources. Scalability and generalizability to other domains remain concerns.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation of foundation models for mathematical reasoning in visual contexts. Benchmark for evaluating LLMs and LMMs capabilities in solving rigorous reasoning tasks. Model development validation using testmini subset.
